newsitem.title: UK: Manufacturing orders up in most UK regions - CBI.
newsitem.headline: Manufacturing orders up in most UK regions - CBI.

text.p: Orders for manufactured goods rose modestly in nine of the 11 UK regions in the four months to April, with the North and East Anglia seeing the greatest increase, a Confederation of British Industry business survey said on Tuesday.
"The rise in orders has been based on growth in domestic demand off-setting weak export orders due to the strength of sterling," the influential CBI said in its quarterly Regional Trends survey.

The report supports the findings of the CBI's national quarterly trends survey which two weeks ago showed domestic demand for British manufactured goods rose at the fastest rate for two years for the four months to April while export orders fell back.

Sterling has rocketed almost 19 percent on a trade weighted basis since last August, threatening the competitiveness of British good abroad. The regional report showed manufacturers in all regions except the East Midlands cut their export prices over the last four months in a effort to combat sterling's appreciation.

But export orders fell, despite lower sterling prices. The largest price falls over the last four months were seen in Northern Ireland and East Anglia. Only firms in Scotland and Wales reported higher export orders.
The outlook for exports offered little encouragement, the CBI said.

"Optimism about exports for the coming year has fallen in all regions except Scotland and Northern Ireland, with manufacturers in the North reporting the biggest fall in export confidence," the survey said.

Manufacturing output continued to grow in most regions over the last four months, reflecting the increase in orders. Only three regions -- Northern Ireland, East Anglia and the North West -- did not achieve growth.
The survey showed little change in the national price level, though domestic prices were cut by firms in the North, East Anglia and the North West.
And despite the fall in export confidence, manufacturers were positive about the outlook for the domestic market.
"Firms in East Anglia, Scotland and Wales reported strong rises in business confidence since January," the survey said.
The survey covered 1,060 manufacturing firms and was carried out between March 21 and April 9.
